questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must not drive faster than is reasonable and safe. You must adjust your speed based on traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and light. You must also obey posted speed limits.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in how far your vehicle takes to stop?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These factors change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph may need up to ____ feet to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Tractor-trailers take much longer to stop than regular cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph may need almost 400 feet to stop.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane that matches the arrow direction.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for the turn. Let any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection cross first.

questions.question: When entering the interstate with a short entrance ramp and no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Go directly into the right lane and speed up to match traffic flow.
Use the highway shoulder to build up speed.
Speed up only after you see a gap in traffic, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you see a gap in traffic, then enter.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic before speeding up and entering. You should stay stopped while you look for a safe gap.

questions.question: It is legal to drive faster than the speed limit when passing another vehicle.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You can never go faster than the posted speed limit, even when passing another vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Turn the wheel sharply in the opposite direction.
Turn your steering wheel toward traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer in the same direction as the skid.

questions.question: A solid white line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving the same direction. A solid white line means drivers cannot pass.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only look in your mirrors.
Start signaling as you move into the new lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles can hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before you change lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on residential streets, or five seconds before changing lanes on freeways.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turns are not allowed here.
You can turn left only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turns are not allowed here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is prohibited. This sign means left turns are not permitted.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: They are placed wherever there is danger.
They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what to do or not do in an area. They show speed limits, no passing rules, or other driving rules.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get in a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable and can see the road. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel once your seat is set.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, what should you do?

options.text: Turn into any lane.
Turn into the first lane.
Turn into the second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the first lane.
questions.explanation: When turning, always turn from your lane into the first available legal lane. When turning from a two-way to a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you slow down?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Stay at highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off your ignition carefully so the steering wheel does not lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully so the steering wheel does not lock.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, the car will keep going fast even with your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition carefully by moving the switch only enough to stop the engine. Do not lock the steering wheel. Then use your brakes and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you the road will curve right first, then curve left. Slow down to safely handle these curves.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through it.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through it.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot get all the way through. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what is best?

options.text: Go slowly while waiting for an opening.
Speed up faster than freeway traffic.
Turn on hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic so you can blend in smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?

options.text: You are not required to stop.
You must slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see at least 200 feet in both directions, even if you enter the intersection.
Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop closest to the intersecting road where you can see traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look left and right to see what is coming.
Pass slowly by cars that seem stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross or enter your path, look left and right to make sure nothing is coming.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, what should you do?

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights or a siren, you must move out of the way. Drive to the right side of the road as far as safely possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop if cars are coming.
Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Go slowly through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only if traffic is on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must stop completely. Let vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their bright headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the oncoming vehicle.
Toward the right edge of the road.
Toward the left edge of the road.
Straight ahead down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right edge of the road if an oncoming car has bright lights on. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see the road well enough to stay in your lane.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down.
Flash your headlights.
Use a quick, loud horn blast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a quick, loud horn blast.
questions.explanation: When a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your car, use a quick, loud horn blast to warn them.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Do not brake.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not use the brakes. Braking will make the skid worse.
